major_concerns: Representativeness of the 200 intent tasks (synthetic vs realistic) may limit external validity.
Strength and coverage of the deterministic verifier must be detailed — weak verifiers will bias pass-rate conclusions.
Prompt sensitivity and hidden-system prompts could change iteration dynamics; single-model design constrains generality.
Handling and detection of oscillatory/divergent repair traces needs explicit, pre-registered criteria to avoid post-hoc selection.
API rate limits and transient provider failures could bias latency and model-call cost measurements if not carefully logged and handled.
required_design_repairs: Specify canonical sources and sampling strategy for the 200 intents and include a realism/coverage justification (or a small human-validated holdout).
Define the deterministic verifier (tool, version, exact checks) and its known limitations; include unit tests demonstrating verifier behavior on canonical cases.
Pre-register formal oscillation/divergence detection rules (e.g., edit-distance cycles, semantic-equivalence thresholds) and exclusion policies.
Include at least one model-sensitivity check (second model or model-temperature perturbation) or justify single-model choice.
Preregister explicit retry and infrastructure-failure handling policies and collect provider-metadata (timestamps, error codes) for bias analysis.

major_concerns: Public-release feasibility given operator privacy/legal constraints is unclear and must be concretely addressed.
Synthetic/curated data may not capture production diversity; benchmark risk of encouraging formatting or template overfitting.
Canonical vendor variants (IOS/JUNOS) require expert validation—risk of subtle semantic mismatches across vendor syntaxes.
Metric design (pass/fail boolean) may oversimplify operational correctness unless supplemented with richer diagnostic labels and trace semantics.
required_design_repairs: Provide a concrete anonymization and legal-risk mitigation plan (examples, licenses, provenance and synthetic augmentation policy).
Describe the canonical-configuration creation process and include expert validation (or an inter-annotator agreement report) for a representative subset.
Expand verifier outputs to include structured diagnostic labels and a taxonomy; preregister labeling rules to avoid ad-hoc post hoc categorization.
Add adversarial-formatting and surface-hack detection controls (e.g., whitespace-insensitive verification, parse-level checks) to prevent gaming.
Supply a small baseline prompt bank and deterministic evaluation harness with checksums and environment manifests to ensure reproducibility.

major_concerns: Simulator fidelity: lightweight simulators may misclassify outage risk relative to real deployments—threat to construct and external validity.
Agent orchestration details (tool APIs, prompting for repairs, deterministic behavior) must be fully specified to permit causal attribution.
Definition and operationalization of 'high-impact misconfiguration' must be preregistered (outage thresholds, path disruption metrics).
Latency and cost trade-offs may make augmentation impractical; needs concrete latency budgets and operational use-case framing.
required_design_repairs: Preregister the exact simulator and verifier implementations, versions, deterministic seeds, and validation tests comparing simulator outputs to known ground truths.
Define formal outage/impact metrics (e.g., fraction of destination pairs losing connectivity, prefix reachability thresholds) and decision thresholds.
Specify the agent/tool interface, prompts for repair, and deterministic control (e.g., temperature=0) to allow causal claims about augmentation.
Include an ablation that separates verifier-only, simulator-only, and full-agent pipelines to isolate sources of improvement.
Preregister latency budgets and report end-to-end wall-clock times including tool call overhead; plan for rate-limit logging and mitigation.

major_concerns: Hidden/system prompts, model-side normalization, and tokenization differences can confound attribution of observed sensitivity to user-visible prompt changes.
Selecting three hosted LLMs without documenting exact model identifiers/versions undermines reproducibility and interpretability.
Prompt-normalization risks overfitting to the chosen dataset and vendor variants; generalization must be demonstrated or bounded.
Statistical power and multiplicity control must be specified given many templates × models × tasks comparisons.
required_design_repairs: Preregister exact model identifiers, versions, and provider metadata; include a short explanation if constrained by provider naming policies.
Add controls for hidden prompts/system messages (where possible) and document tokenization-aware comparisons or normalization procedures.
Specify multiplicity adjustments and sample-size calculations / power analysis for mixed-effects models and permutation tests.
Define the prompt-normalization procedure formally and include evaluation on held-out vendor/CLI variants to measure generalization.
Include low-level synthetic control tasks that isolate prompt-token effects (e.g., token-order swaps with semantically invariant intents).
